verdict.rationale: Feitian documents an OpenSK hardware variant that runs firmware built unmodified from Google's open-source OpenSK repository, so for that SKU the code on the device is open and user-buildable. It is framed as a way "to experience and try FIDO authentications." Nothing shows the mainstream BioPass or MultiPass keys run open-source or audited firmware. Missing for 10: open-source or audited firmware for the main production key lines, any independent security audit or certification report, independent or hands-on corroboration, and a way to verify the firmware on shipped devices.

support.subject: As a security engineer, the firmware is open source or independently audited, so I don't have to take the vendor's word for what runs on the device

citations.quote: Users can build firmware from the source code of Google OpenSK Github repository without changing anything, provision it to this OpenSK hardware, to experience and try FIDO authentications.
